meta.what: Instructions executed inside the generated Rust serialize/deserialize, counted by cachegrind and attributed per function by cg_annotate.
meta.why_this_unit: Three idle runs and three on a 6x oversubscribed container reported identical counts to the digit, where a wall-clock sample of the same binary spread 1.41x across twenty runs. A deterministic measurement can carry a 1% budget; a wall-clock one cannot carry 15%.
meta.iterations: The gate's own counts (2000/1000/500), independent of the timing benchmark's, so tuning that one does not silently re-baseline this one. One run costs about a second under cachegrind.
meta.rebaseline_when: A deliberate codegen change, or a rustc upgrade. Both move the count, and both are visible events rather than flakes. Re-baseline in the commit that causes it.
meta.arch_keys: cmake_host_system_information OS_PLATFORM -- 'aarch64', 'x86_64'. Counts are per-architecture because the instruction streams differ. An architecture with no entry SKIPS and prints the value to paste; it never passes on another architecture's number.
